name: Obscure History Horrors
description: Fifty list categories of obscure and grim history — folklore creatures, the deadliest weapons, warriors, diseases and disasters, the dumbest wars, the myths everyone still repeats, the worst times and places to be alive, and six lives told in the second person from enrolment to grave. Each category carries twenty materially distinct entries, and every entry is written to stand alone twice over: as one item in a ten-minute list, and as one long quiet chapter in a two-hour compilation.

exclusions: No dwelling on suffering: state briefly what happened to a body and then give the procedure, the record, the aftermath or the change in the law the time instead.
No invented quotations, invented documents, invented scenes, or reconstructed dialogue; describe only what the record supports and say plainly where the record stops.
No living people are named, and no living private individual is described, alluded to, or made identifiable by their role, family, employer, or address.
No third-party characters, franchises, brands, product names, logos, or channel names anywhere in an entry.
No death toll, date, distance, or sum is stated more precisely than the record allows, and a contested figure is given as contested rather than picked.
No entry describes a folkloric creature as though it were established fact; the belief is the subject and it is always attributed to the people who held it.
No blaming of a modern nation, people, religion, or party for a historical event, and no modern political analogy of any kind.
No hooks, cliffhangers, countdowns to a worst entry, teasers, questions to the listener, or promises about what is coming later.
Keep every entry self-contained, resolving to a quiet close, with no reference forward to a later entry and no callback to an earlier one.
No entry is left at the myth: where the popular version is known to be wrong, the correction is given plainly and early rather than saved for an ending.
prompt_context: Every entry is built the same way: the thing, then what actually happened, then what it cost and what changed. Name the thing plainly in the first sentence — the creature, the weapon, the disease, the disaster, the war, the myth, the year, the moment in a life — and say what it is before saying anything about how strange or awful it was. The material here is grim by nature and it is told without relish: describe injury, disease, killing and ruin briefly and factually, and give the aftermath, the procedure, the inquiry, the record or the change in the law more room than the event itself. Nothing is dwelt on, nothing is lingered over, and no entry is written to make a listener wince. Where the subject is a folkloric creature, the belief is the subject: say who held it, where, and what the belief was doing for them — a hazard marked, a rule enforced, a loss made bearable — and never present the creature as an established fact. Where the subject is a myth that people still repeat, give the correction plainly and early; an entry that saves the correction for a final line has been written as a hook and is wrong. Where a life is told in the second person, keep the second person steady and unsentimental, build it out of the ordinary and documented details of that life, and end each stage where the record ends rather than in an imagined scene. Invent nothing: no reconstructed dialogue, no imagined interiors, no confident figure the record cannot support, and no source cited by title. Every entry must work at both of this pack's two speeds. Read quickly it is one item in a list of twenty; read slowly it is a chapter of an hour, and the extra time is spent on detail — the wording of a regulation, the size of a search area, the price of a bushel, the depth of a seam — never on tension, atmosphere or a raised voice. Keep every entry self-contained, and end each one on something still: a closed inquiry, a repealed statute, a stone with a number on it, a register entry that has not changed in a century.

idea_axes.label: Entry lens
values: the thing itself, described plainly and without atmosphere
the place it belonged to, and why it belonged there and nowhere else
the mechanism, and what it was actually doing for the people involved
the record, and exactly how much of it survives
the correction, given early, where a popular version is wrong
the cost, counted in the units the record actually used
the change that followed, in law, practice, or building
the ending, and whether anyone noticed it at the time

idea_axes.label: Entry shape
values: the thing, then what happened, then what changed
the belief, then the people who held it, then what it was for
the claim, then the record, then the correction
one document read closely, and what it settles
one stage of a life, told in the second person and closed quietly

idea_axes.label: Runtime mode
values: short list mode: one entry in a minute or two, at a normal narrating pace
sleep compilation mode: one entry as a long quiet chapter at a slower pace

tuples.episode_object: the deficiency illness common in one milling region
tuples.time_place_scope: a district where a grain was processed in a particular way
tuples.mechanism: a disease created by a processing method and cured by reversing it
tuples.evidence_lens: the milling records compared with the regional health returns

tuples.episode_object: the disease that left once a parasite's host was controlled
tuples.time_place_scope: an area where an intermediate host was eliminated
tuples.mechanism: an illness ended by ecology rather than by medicine
tuples.evidence_lens: the ecological survey compared with the infection rates recorded

tuples.episode_object: the illness recorded only in one profession
tuples.time_place_scope: a trade that used a specific material daily
tuples.mechanism: a disease so localised it disappears with a single workplace's closure
tuples.evidence_lens: the trade records compared with the medical officer's returns

tuples.episode_object: the fever that stopped after a mass treatment campaign
tuples.time_place_scope: a region where the whole population was treated at once
tuples.mechanism: an intervention that breaks a transmission cycle rather than treating individuals
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign records compared with the incidence figures

tuples.episode_object: the illness whose insect vector was eliminated locally
tuples.time_place_scope: a district subject to a sustained control programme
tuples.mechanism: a disappearance that must be maintained, and that returns when the programme stops
tuples.evidence_lens: the vector survey compared with the case returns across the programme's life

tuples.episode_object: the disease that ended when an import was prohibited
tuples.time_place_scope: a port that stopped receiving a particular cargo
tuples.mechanism: a health outcome produced entirely by a customs decision
tuples.evidence_lens: the customs records compared with the disease notifications

tuples.episode_object: the illness that was eliminated in one country only
tuples.time_place_scope: a nation that achieved control while its neighbours did not
tuples.mechanism: an elimination that depends on a border, which is not a stable thing to depend on
tuples.evidence_lens: the national surveillance records compared with the neighbouring returns

tuples.episode_object: the condition that turned out to have an environmental cause
tuples.time_place_scope: a district with a distinctive local water chemistry
tuples.mechanism: an illness explained by geology, which is why it appeared in one valley and not the next
tuples.evidence_lens: the geological survey compared with the case distribution map

coverage_profiles.subject: the deadliest single days in history

tuples.episode_object: the day a volcanic island collapsed into the sea
tuples.time_place_scope: an archipelago where the sea travelled to inhabited coasts
tuples.mechanism: a single event whose death toll is almost entirely from the water it displaced
tuples.evidence_lens: the tide gauge records compared with the coastal casualty returns

tuples.episode_object: the day an earthquake struck a city at breakfast
tuples.time_place_scope: an urban area built largely in unreinforced masonry
tuples.mechanism: a timing that puts the whole population indoors, which decides the toll before the shaking starts
tuples.evidence_lens: the building survey compared with the hour recorded on the stopped clocks

tuples.episode_object: the day a cyclone came ashore on a low delta
tuples.time_place_scope: a densely settled coast barely above sea level
tuples.mechanism: a storm surge in a place with no high ground, which is a geography problem more than a weather one
tuples.evidence_lens: the elevation survey compared with the surge height recorded

tuples.episode_object: the day a dam failed above a valley town
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement in a narrow valley below a reservoir
tuples.mechanism: an engineering failure whose toll is set by the valley's shape
tuples.evidence_lens: the dam inquiry report compared with the settlement's population records

tuples.episode_object: the day a fire crossed a city's firebreaks
tuples.time_place_scope: a town built of timber in a dry season with a high wind
tuples.mechanism: a fire that stops being fought and starts being fled, which changes the toll by an order of magnitude
tuples.evidence_lens: the fire service records compared with the burial registers

tuples.episode_object: the day a flood wave reached a river city
tuples.time_place_scope: a river system that had received rain across its whole catchment
tuples.mechanism: a flood produced upstream and delivered downstream, which arrives without local warning
tuples.evidence_lens: the rainfall records compared with the river gauge series

tuples.episode_object: the day a landslide buried a settlement
tuples.time_place_scope: a village built at the foot of an unstable slope
tuples.mechanism: a hazard visible on a map for decades, and acted on afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the geological survey compared with the settlement's building history

tuples.episode_object: the day a mine gas explosion reached the workings
tuples.time_place_scope: a colliery working a seam known for firedamp
tuples.mechanism: a hazard managed daily until the management fails once
tuples.evidence_lens: the mine inspection records compared with the inquiry findings

tuples.episode_object: the day a passenger ship sank in cold water
tuples.time_place_scope: a crossing where survival time in the water was minutes
tuples.mechanism: a toll set by water temperature and boat capacity rather than by the sinking itself
tuples.evidence_lens: the ship's boat capacity compared with the survivor list

tuples.episode_object: the day a tsunami crossed an ocean basin
tuples.time_place_scope: coastlines thousands of miles from the source event
tuples.mechanism: a hazard that arrives hours later at places that felt nothing
tuples.evidence_lens: the seismic records compared with the arrival times logged along each coast

tuples.episode_object: the day a heat event broke a regional record
tuples.time_place_scope: a densely built city with little shade and no cooling
tuples.mechanism: a disaster with no visible damage, which is why it is counted late and undercounted
tuples.evidence_lens: the excess mortality analysis compared with the temperature series

tuples.episode_object: the day a storm caught a fishing fleet at sea
tuples.time_place_scope: a fleet working a distant ground in a short season
tuples.mechanism: a total loss concentrated in one community, which loses a generation of men in a night
tuples.evidence_lens: the fleet register compared with the parish burial records

tuples.episode_object: the day a bridge failed under a train
tuples.time_place_scope: a crossing exposed to wind above its design assumptions
tuples.mechanism: a structural failure whose inquiry rewrote a whole engineering practice
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquiry report compared with the bridge's original design calculations

tuples.episode_object: the day a chemical release reached a sleeping city
tuples.time_place_scope: a plant sited beside dense residential housing
tuples.mechanism: a siting decision that determines the toll years before the release
tuples.evidence_lens: the plant siting records compared with the casualty distribution map

tuples.episode_object: the day a stadium crowd was crushed
tuples.time_place_scope: a venue with fixed barriers and a single entry route
tuples.mechanism: a design failure in a crowd flow, which is almost always known about beforehand
tuples.evidence_lens: the venue safety certificate compared with the inquiry findings

tuples.episode_object: the day a hurricane crossed a barrier island
tuples.time_place_scope: a low island with a single evacuation road
tuples.mechanism: an evacuation capacity problem, which turns a forecast into a toll
tuples.evidence_lens: the evacuation plan compared with the traffic records of the day

tuples.episode_object: the day an avalanche reached a valley road
tuples.time_place_scope: a mountain route kept open through a heavy snow season
tuples.mechanism: a decision to keep a route open, made every winter until one winter it is wrong
tuples.evidence_lens: the avalanche control records compared with the road closure log

tuples.episode_object: the day a ferry capsized on a short crossing
tuples.time_place_scope: a route worked by a vessel loaded beyond its stability limit
tuples.mechanism: an overloading practice tolerated for years, ended in minutes
tuples.evidence_lens: the vessel's stability book compared with the manifest of the day

tuples.episode_object: the day a wildfire ran through a hill town
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement surrounded by fuel with one road out
tuples.mechanism: a wildland interface problem, in which the town is the fuel and the road is the only defence
tuples.evidence_lens: the fuel survey compared with the evacuation timeline

tuples.episode_object: the day a lightning strike ignited a powder store
tuples.time_place_scope: a fortified building holding a very large quantity of explosive
tuples.mechanism: a storage decision whose consequence is total, and which is only ever changed afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the magazine records compared with the damage survey

coverage_profiles.subject: volcanic eruptions that darkened the sky

tuples.episode_object: the eruption followed by a year without a summer
tuples.time_place_scope: a farming world dependent on a single growing season
tuples.mechanism: an aerosol veil that cools a hemisphere, and is only connected to the mountain much later
tuples.evidence_lens: the harvest records compared with the ice core sulphate layer

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that buried two towns under ash
tuples.time_place_scope: a coastal region settled right up to the mountain's foot
tuples.mechanism: a hazard whose warning signs were legible and unread, which is the usual pattern
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation stratigraphy compared with the surviving written account

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that emptied a caldera in days
tuples.time_place_scope: an island volcano with a very large magma chamber
tuples.mechanism: a collapse event, where the mountain's disappearance is the disaster rather than the eruption
tuples.evidence_lens: the bathymetric survey compared with the eruption chronology

tuples.episode_object: the eruption whose ash closed air routes for a week
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern aviation network crossing a volcanic region
tuples.mechanism: a hazard that costs almost nothing in lives and enormous amounts in movement
tuples.evidence_lens: the ash dispersal modelling compared with the flight cancellation records

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that produced a lake of acid
tuples.time_place_scope: a crater that filled with water after the event
tuples.mechanism: a slow hazard created by a fast one, which threatens people who were not born when it erupted
tuples.evidence_lens: the water chemistry monitoring compared with the eruption date

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that released gas from a crater lake
tuples.time_place_scope: a valley where heavy gas could flow downhill and pool
tuples.mechanism: a hazard with no explosion at all, which is why nobody expected it or planned for it
tuples.evidence_lens: the gas concentration measurements compared with the casualty locations

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that generated a mud flow down a valley
tuples.time_place_scope: a snow-capped volcano above a populated river valley
tuples.mechanism: a hazard made of melted ice rather than of lava, and far faster than anyone can walk
tuples.evidence_lens: the valley survey compared with the flow deposit thickness

tuples.episode_object: the eruption preceded by months of small earthquakes
tuples.time_place_scope: a monitored volcano with an established observatory
tuples.mechanism: a warning sequence that was read correctly, which is why this one has a small toll
tuples.evidence_lens: the seismic record compared with the evacuation order dates

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that created a new island
tuples.time_place_scope: a shallow sea above an active vent
tuples.mechanism: a construction event rather than a destruction one, which is rare enough to be studied closely
tuples.evidence_lens: the survey charts compared before and after the event

tuples.episode_object: the eruption whose pumice raft crossed an ocean
tuples.time_place_scope: a sea route where floating rock drifted for months
tuples.mechanism: a hazard to shipping produced by an eruption thousands of miles away
tuples.evidence_lens: the ships' logs compared with the drift modelling

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that ended a settlement permanently
tuples.time_place_scope: an island community that was never resettled afterwards
tuples.mechanism: an event that removes a place from the map, which very few natural events actually do
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlement records compared with the post-eruption survey

tuples.episode_object: the eruption recorded in tree rings across a continent
tuples.time_place_scope: forests growing at their climatic limit
tuples.mechanism: a global signal preserved in wood, which dates an eruption nobody wrote down
tuples.evidence_lens: the tree ring series compared with the ice core record

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that produced coloured sunsets for years
tuples.time_place_scope: an atmosphere loaded with fine particles at high altitude
tuples.mechanism: an optical effect that is the only trace most people ever saw of the event
tuples.evidence_lens: the contemporary observational records compared with the eruption chronology

tuples.episode_object: the eruption whose lava flow was diverted by engineering
tuples.time_place_scope: a town in the path of a slow-moving flow
tuples.mechanism: the rare case where a volcanic hazard can actually be fought, and was
tuples.evidence_lens: the engineering records compared with the flow's mapped path

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that killed mostly from famine afterwards
tuples.time_place_scope: an agricultural region that lost a harvest and its livestock
tuples.mechanism: a death toll that arrives over two years and is attributed to hunger rather than to a mountain
tuples.evidence_lens: the mortality records compared with the eruption date and the harvest returns

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that had been dormant for a millennium
tuples.time_place_scope: a mountain that local knowledge did not treat as a volcano
tuples.mechanism: a hazard forgotten because the interval exceeded human memory
tuples.evidence_lens: the geological dating compared with the settlement pattern on the slopes

tuples.episode_object: the eruption whose pyroclastic flow crossed water
tuples.time_place_scope: a strait narrow enough for a flow to travel over the surface
tuples.mechanism: a behaviour thought impossible until it was observed, which changed hazard mapping everywhere
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposit survey on the far shore compared with the event accounts

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that filled a valley with ash to the rooftops
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement downwind in the prevailing season
tuples.mechanism: a wind direction that decides which villages survive, and which is different each eruption
tuples.evidence_lens: the ash isopach map compared with the settlement damage survey

tuples.episode_object: the eruption monitored continuously from beginning to end
tuples.time_place_scope: a volcano with a dense modern instrument network
tuples.mechanism: the first complete record of a whole cycle, which is what every earlier eruption lacked
tuples.evidence_lens: the instrument record compared with the eruption's mapped products

tuples.episode_object: the eruption that is still going after decades
tuples.time_place_scope: a vent that has been effusing continuously for a very long time
tuples.mechanism: a hazard that becomes a landscape, and eventually a tourist route
tuples.evidence_lens: the effusion rate series compared with the land use records around the vent

coverage_profiles.subject: earthquakes that rewrote a coastline

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that lifted a harbour above the tide
tuples.time_place_scope: a working port whose quays depended on a fixed sea level
tuples.mechanism: an uplift event that destroys a harbour without damaging a single building
tuples.evidence_lens: the harbour survey before and after compared with the levelling records

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that dropped a district below sea level
tuples.time_place_scope: a coastal city built on unconsolidated sediment
tuples.mechanism: a subsidence event that turns a district into a lagoon permanently
tuples.evidence_lens: the levelling survey compared with the flooded area mapped afterwards

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that liquefied a whole suburb
tuples.time_place_scope: a district built on saturated sand and silt
tuples.mechanism: a ground failure where the soil, not the shaking, destroys the buildings
tuples.evidence_lens: the geotechnical survey compared with the damage distribution

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that shifted a river's mouth
tuples.time_place_scope: a delta where a channel could migrate easily
tuples.mechanism: a change in river geometry that redraws a coast and moves a port with it
tuples.evidence_lens: the historic charts compared with the post-event survey

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that raised a series of marine terraces
tuples.time_place_scope: a coast that had recorded earlier uplift in its rock
tuples.mechanism: a repeat event whose predecessors are still visible as steps in the landscape
tuples.evidence_lens: the terrace dating compared with the historical record of the event

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that destroyed a port and moved its trade
tuples.time_place_scope: a region with a second harbour able to absorb the traffic
tuples.mechanism: an economic redistribution caused by a fault, which outlasts the rebuilding
tuples.evidence_lens: the customs records compared with the port damage assessment

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that submerged a settlement's street plan
tuples.time_place_scope: a town whose foundations are now under shallow water
tuples.mechanism: a site preserved by drowning, which is why we know its layout so well
tuples.evidence_lens: the underwater survey compared with the pre-event property records

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that broke a coastal road for a generation
tuples.time_place_scope: a route cut into a cliff above the sea
tuples.mechanism: an infrastructure loss that isolates communities far longer than the shaking lasted
tuples.evidence_lens: the road repair records compared with the settlement census returns

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake felt across a whole continent
tuples.time_place_scope: a large event in a region of very efficient wave propagation
tuples.mechanism: an event whose reach reveals the structure of the crust it travelled through
tuples.evidence_lens: the felt reports compared with the modern attenuation models

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that produced a wave in an enclosed sea
tuples.time_place_scope: a basin where a wave could reflect and return
tuples.mechanism: a hazard that arrives twice, which catches people who had already returned to the shore
tuples.evidence_lens: the tide gauge trace compared with the casualty timing

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that triggered an underwater landslide
tuples.time_place_scope: a steep continental slope loaded with sediment
tuples.mechanism: a secondary hazard that produces the wave, so the fault is not the direct cause at all
tuples.evidence_lens: the seafloor survey compared with the wave arrival times

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that changed a spring's flow permanently
tuples.time_place_scope: a district dependent on a small number of springs
tuples.mechanism: a hydrological change that alters where people can live, long after the rebuilding
tuples.evidence_lens: the spring discharge records compared with the settlement pattern

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that broke a submarine cable network
tuples.time_place_scope: a seafloor carrying several communication routes
tuples.mechanism: a modern hazard, in which a slope failure severs a continent's connections
tuples.evidence_lens: the cable fault locations compared with the turbidity current modelling

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that revealed an unmapped fault
tuples.time_place_scope: a region considered stable before the event
tuples.mechanism: a hazard assessment corrected by the event it failed to predict
tuples.evidence_lens: the pre-event hazard map compared with the surface rupture survey

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake with a surface rupture across a road
tuples.time_place_scope: a fault crossing a made landscape of fences and roads
tuples.mechanism: a rupture measurable to the centimetre because human lines crossed it
tuples.evidence_lens: the road survey compared with the offset measured on the ground

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that damaged buildings only on one soil type
tuples.time_place_scope: a city built across two very different foundation materials
tuples.mechanism: a damage pattern that maps geology rather than construction quality
tuples.evidence_lens: the soil map compared with the building damage survey

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake followed by a long aftershock sequence
tuples.time_place_scope: a region where the sequence lasted longer than the rebuilding
tuples.mechanism: an event that prevents recovery by never quite finishing
tuples.evidence_lens: the aftershock catalogue compared with the reconstruction timeline

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake that changed a country's building code
tuples.time_place_scope: a nation that rebuilt to a new standard afterwards
tuples.mechanism: the one durable product of a disaster, which is measured in the next event's toll
tuples.evidence_lens: the code revision documents compared with the damage figures of the following event

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake recorded by an instrument for the first time
tuples.time_place_scope: a period when seismographs were newly installed
tuples.mechanism: the beginning of a quantitative record, which is why everything earlier is estimated
tuples.evidence_lens: the instrument trace compared with the felt intensity reports

tuples.episode_object: the earthquake known only from a raised beach
tuples.time_place_scope: a coast with no written record for the period
tuples.mechanism: an event dated by shellfish and driftwood, which is how most of the record was made
tuples.evidence_lens: the radiocarbon dates compared with the elevation of the beach deposit

coverage_profiles.subject: floods that moved a river permanently

tuples.episode_object: the flood that cut a new channel across a meander
tuples.time_place_scope: a lowland river with a tight loop and a low neck
tuples.mechanism: an avulsion that shortens a river overnight and strands a port on a dry bend
tuples.evidence_lens: the historic charts compared with the post-flood survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that abandoned a delta distributary
tuples.time_place_scope: a delta where the flow could choose between several routes
tuples.mechanism: a channel switch that moves a whole coastline's sediment supply
tuples.evidence_lens: the sediment core dating compared with the historical navigation records

tuples.episode_object: the flood that breached a levee and kept the breach
tuples.time_place_scope: a river confined between artificial banks for centuries
tuples.mechanism: an engineering system that fails at its weakest point and then defines the new river
tuples.evidence_lens: the levee inspection records compared with the breach survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that filled an old channel long thought dead
tuples.time_place_scope: a floodplain still carrying the scar of a former course
tuples.mechanism: a river remembering a route, which is why old channels are the worst places to build
tuples.evidence_lens: the geomorphological map compared with the flood extent recorded

tuples.episode_object: the flood that moved a ford and closed a market town
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement that existed because of a single crossing
tuples.mechanism: an economic collapse caused by a hydrological change, and never reversed
tuples.evidence_lens: the market charter records compared with the crossing's later condition

tuples.episode_object: the flood that destroyed a bridge and its town
tuples.time_place_scope: a crossing where the bridge had constrained the channel
tuples.mechanism: a structure that made the flood worse, which is how many river towns were lost
tuples.evidence_lens: the bridge design records compared with the scour survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that reversed a canal's usefulness
tuples.time_place_scope: a canal built to the level of the pre-flood river
tuples.mechanism: an infrastructure investment stranded by a change in the river it was built beside
tuples.evidence_lens: the canal company records compared with the river level series

tuples.episode_object: the flood that deposited a metre of silt on a floodplain
tuples.time_place_scope: a farming district whose soil was suddenly different
tuples.mechanism: a disaster that improves the land, which is why people came back within a year
tuples.evidence_lens: the soil survey compared with the yield records before and after

tuples.episode_object: the flood that drowned a lower town and left an upper one
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement built in two tiers on a valley side
tuples.mechanism: a topographic accident that decides which half of a town survives
tuples.evidence_lens: the elevation survey compared with the damage distribution

tuples.episode_object: the flood that came from a lake released upstream
tuples.time_place_scope: a valley below a natural dam of ice or landslide debris
tuples.mechanism: an outburst flood, which arrives without rain and cannot be forecast from the weather
tuples.evidence_lens: the dam remnant survey compared with the flood deposit downstream

tuples.episode_object: the flood that changed a national border
tuples.time_place_scope: two states divided by a river channel
tuples.mechanism: a legal problem created by physics, and argued over for a century afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the boundary treaty text compared with the post-flood channel survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that ended a fishery on one bank
tuples.time_place_scope: a river whose spawning gravels were buried by sediment
tuples.mechanism: an ecological loss produced by a single event and lasting decades
tuples.evidence_lens: the catch records compared with the substrate survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that filled a mine's workings
tuples.time_place_scope: a colliery driven under a river's floodplain
tuples.mechanism: an industrial hazard created by pumping until the pumping stops
tuples.evidence_lens: the mine plans compared with the flood level records

tuples.episode_object: the flood that stranded a port miles from the sea
tuples.time_place_scope: a harbour on a channel that filled with sediment
tuples.mechanism: a slow ending accelerated by one event, which is how most inland ports die
tuples.evidence_lens: the port trade records compared with the channel depth surveys

tuples.episode_object: the flood that produced a permanent lake
tuples.time_place_scope: a valley whose outlet was blocked by debris
tuples.mechanism: a landscape change that adds a water body to a map and never removes it
tuples.evidence_lens: the pre-flood mapping compared with the modern topographic survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that overtopped a defence built for a lesser event
tuples.time_place_scope: a district protected to a design standard set decades earlier
tuples.mechanism: a design assumption outlived by the climate it was written for
tuples.evidence_lens: the design calculations compared with the recorded flood level

tuples.episode_object: the flood that moved a fishing village to higher ground
tuples.time_place_scope: a community that rebuilt somewhere else entirely
tuples.mechanism: a relocation decision made once, which is rarer than it should be
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlement records compared with the flood extent map

tuples.episode_object: the flood that exposed an earlier settlement
tuples.time_place_scope: a bank cut back to reveal older occupation layers
tuples.mechanism: an archaeological gift delivered by a disaster, and usually washed away soon after
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation record compared with the erosion survey

tuples.episode_object: the flood that silted a navigation for a generation
tuples.time_place_scope: a river carrying trade upstream to inland towns
tuples.mechanism: a transport route closed by mud, and reopened only when dredging became affordable
tuples.evidence_lens: the navigation authority records compared with the dredging accounts

tuples.episode_object: the flood recorded on a wall by successive marks
tuples.time_place_scope: a town that kept a public record of every high water
tuples.mechanism: a data series created by ordinary people, which is often better than the official one
tuples.evidence_lens: the flood marks compared with the modern gauge record

coverage_profiles.subject: fires that took a whole city

tuples.episode_object: the fire that started in a bakery and spread on a wind
tuples.time_place_scope: a city of timber-framed houses with overhanging upper floors
tuples.mechanism: a building style that puts fuel above the street, so a fire travels along the roofline
tuples.evidence_lens: the building survey compared with the fire's mapped spread

tuples.episode_object: the fire that jumped a river on burning debris
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement on both banks of a narrow channel
tuples.mechanism: a firebreak defeated by embers, which is how most firebreaks are defeated
tuples.evidence_lens: the wind records compared with the ignition points on the far bank

tuples.episode_object: the fire that followed an earthquake
tuples.time_place_scope: a city whose water mains broke in the same minute
tuples.mechanism: a secondary disaster that causes most of the damage attributed to the first
tuples.evidence_lens: the water main survey compared with the fire's spread map

tuples.episode_object: the fire in a warehouse district full of oil
tuples.time_place_scope: a port storing bulk flammable cargo close to housing
tuples.mechanism: a siting decision that concentrates fuel where people live
tuples.evidence_lens: the warehouse inventories compared with the fire investigation

tuples.episode_object: the fire that could not be fought for want of water
tuples.time_place_scope: a town whose supply was a single tank filled by hand
tuples.mechanism: a fire service defeated by hydraulics rather than by courage
tuples.evidence_lens: the water supply records compared with the fire brigade's own report

tuples.episode_object: the fire that spread through a shared roof void
tuples.time_place_scope: a terrace of buildings with a continuous unbroken roof space
tuples.mechanism: a construction detail that turns twenty buildings into one
tuples.evidence_lens: the building plans compared with the damage survey

tuples.episode_object: the fire that a change in wind saved half a city from
tuples.time_place_scope: a fire front that turned ninety degrees in an hour
tuples.mechanism: a survival decided by weather, which is why the surviving half is entirely arbitrary
tuples.evidence_lens: the meteorological record compared with the burnt area boundary

tuples.episode_object: the fire that destroyed a city's records
tuples.time_place_scope: a municipal archive stored in one building
tuples.mechanism: a loss that makes the fire itself harder to study than it should be
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving duplicate records compared with the catalogue of what was lost

tuples.episode_object: the fire that led to the first building regulations
tuples.time_place_scope: a rebuilding programme carried out under new rules
tuples.mechanism: a regulation written in the ruins, which is when regulations are actually possible
tuples.evidence_lens: the rebuilding statutes compared with the pre-fire building survey

tuples.episode_object: the fire that started in a theatre
tuples.time_place_scope: a public building with inward-opening doors and one stair
tuples.mechanism: an evacuation failure designed into a building years before the fire
tuples.evidence_lens: the building plans compared with the inquest findings

tuples.episode_object: the fire that ran through a dockside of tarred rope
tuples.time_place_scope: a working port storing ships' stores in bulk
tuples.mechanism: a fuel load nobody thought of as a fuel load until it burned
tuples.evidence_lens: the stores inventory compared with the fire's origin analysis

tuples.episode_object: the fire that a firebreak actually stopped
tuples.time_place_scope: a city where buildings were pulled down ahead of the flames
tuples.mechanism: the rare case where a deliberate demolition worked, and the argument it caused afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the demolition orders compared with the burnt area boundary

tuples.episode_object: the fire started by a lamp in a stable
tuples.time_place_scope: a district where animals were kept between houses
tuples.mechanism: a mixed land use that puts an ignition source in the middle of a residential block
tuples.evidence_lens: the property records compared with the fire's origin point

tuples.episode_object: the fire that burned for days in a coal seam under a town
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement built above a shallow worked seam
tuples.mechanism: a fire that cannot be fought at all, and that ends the town by outlasting it
tuples.evidence_lens: the mine plans compared with the subsidence and temperature surveys

tuples.episode_object: the fire that destroyed a fleet at its moorings
tuples.time_place_scope: a harbour where ships lay close together in a light wind
tuples.mechanism: a concentration of value in one place, which is what a harbour is for
tuples.evidence_lens: the harbour master's records compared with the loss returns

tuples.episode_object: the fire that was blamed on the wrong people
tuples.time_place_scope: a city already carrying a political or religious tension
tuples.mechanism: a disaster used as an occasion, which the investigation record usually contradicts
tuples.evidence_lens: the judicial proceedings compared with the fire investigation findings

tuples.episode_object: the fire that led a city to build a water main network
tuples.time_place_scope: a municipality that borrowed heavily to install pressure mains
tuples.mechanism: an infrastructure decision that only becomes affordable after a catastrophe
tuples.evidence_lens: the municipal borrowing records compared with the fire loss assessment

tuples.episode_object: the fire that emptied a district permanently
tuples.time_place_scope: a neighbourhood that was cleared rather than rebuilt
tuples.mechanism: a disaster used to complete a redevelopment that was already being argued about
tuples.evidence_lens: the redevelopment proposals compared with the fire's boundary

tuples.episode_object: the fire in a factory with locked exits
tuples.time_place_scope: a workplace where doors were secured against theft
tuples.mechanism: a management decision that becomes the cause of death, and is found in the inquest every time
tuples.evidence_lens: the workplace inspection record compared with the inquest evidence

tuples.episode_object: the fire that produced the first insurance brigade
tuples.time_place_scope: a city where insurers marked and defended their own buildings
tuples.mechanism: a private fire service, which explains a great deal about why public ones were created
tuples.evidence_lens: the insurance company records compared with the buildings marked

coverage_profiles.subject: famines caused by a decision rather than a harvest

tuples.episode_object: the famine during which food was still being exported
tuples.time_place_scope: a region producing a surplus of one crop and starving on another
tuples.mechanism: a distribution failure rather than a production failure, which is the commonest kind
tuples.evidence_lens: the export returns compared with the mortality records of the same months

tuples.episode_object: the famine created by a change in landholding
tuples.time_place_scope: a countryside where subsistence plots were consolidated
tuples.mechanism: a policy that removes the margin people were living on before the harvest ever fails
tuples.evidence_lens: the land records compared with the relief applications

tuples.episode_object: the famine deepened by a transport bottleneck
tuples.time_place_scope: a district with grain a hundred miles away and no way to move it
tuples.mechanism: a logistics failure that turns a shortage into a catastrophe
tuples.evidence_lens: the transport records compared with the regional price series

tuples.episode_object: the famine in which relief was made conditional
tuples.time_place_scope: a jurisdiction where aid required a test of destitution
tuples.mechanism: an administrative rule that delays help until the applicant is beyond helping
tuples.evidence_lens: the relief board minutes compared with the workhouse admission records

tuples.episode_object: the famine caused by a requisition quota
tuples.time_place_scope: a rural region required to deliver a fixed amount regardless of yield
tuples.mechanism: a quota set on paper that ignores the harvest, which is the purest form of this category
tuples.evidence_lens: the requisition orders compared with the recorded yields

tuples.episode_object: the famine that followed a currency collapse
tuples.time_place_scope: an economy where food existed but money did not buy it
tuples.mechanism: a monetary failure with a nutritional outcome, which is invisible in the harvest figures
tuples.evidence_lens: the price series compared with the wage records

tuples.episode_object: the famine worsened by a market corner
tuples.time_place_scope: a district where a small number of traders held the stock
tuples.mechanism: a market structure that converts scarcity into profit and profit into more scarcity
tuples.evidence_lens: the merchants' ledgers compared with the local price movements

tuples.episode_object: the famine created by a blockade
tuples.time_place_scope: a population dependent on imported staple food
tuples.mechanism: a deliberate interruption of supply, whose effects are counted long afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the shipping records compared with the mortality returns

tuples.episode_object: the famine that followed a livestock cull
tuples.time_place_scope: a pastoral community whose animals were removed by order
tuples.mechanism: a policy that destroys a food store as well as a herd
tuples.evidence_lens: the cull records compared with the subsequent nutrition surveys

tuples.episode_object: the famine in which a substitute food failed
tuples.time_place_scope: a population moved onto an unfamiliar staple
tuples.mechanism: a nutritional gap created by a substitution nobody tested first
tuples.evidence_lens: the ration composition records compared with the deficiency disease returns

tuples.episode_object: the famine hidden by an optimistic official report
tuples.time_place_scope: an administration whose local officers reported upward
tuples.mechanism: an information failure, which delays relief until the reporting chain is bypassed
tuples.evidence_lens: the official reports compared with the independent observers' accounts

tuples.episode_object: the famine that followed a war's requisitioning
tuples.time_place_scope: a countryside stripped of draught animals and seed corn
tuples.mechanism: a loss of the means of the next harvest, which makes year two worse than year one
tuples.evidence_lens: the requisition records compared with the following year's sown acreage

tuples.episode_object: the famine ended by a single administrative decision
tuples.time_place_scope: a jurisdiction where a rule was suspended and food moved
tuples.mechanism: a demonstration that the constraint was never physical
tuples.evidence_lens: the order suspending the rule compared with the mortality curve

tuples.episode_object: the famine in which the poorest crop failed first
tuples.time_place_scope: a district where the poor ate one crop and the rich another
tuples.mechanism: a class-specific failure, which is why the aggregate harvest figures show nothing
tuples.evidence_lens: the crop returns by type compared with the mortality by district

tuples.episode_object: the famine that produced a mass migration
tuples.time_place_scope: a region whose population left rather than waited
tuples.mechanism: an outcome that removes the famine by removing the population
tuples.evidence_lens: the emigration records compared with the census returns

tuples.episode_object: the famine in which relief works exhausted the workers
tuples.time_place_scope: a scheme requiring heavy labour in exchange for food
tuples.mechanism: a relief design that costs more calories than it delivers
tuples.evidence_lens: the works records compared with the medical officers' reports

tuples.episode_object: the famine caused by a failed irrigation system
tuples.time_place_scope: a district dependent on a canal network in disrepair
tuples.mechanism: an infrastructure failure with a two-season lag before it kills anyone
tuples.evidence_lens: the canal maintenance records compared with the irrigated area returns

tuples.episode_object: the famine that followed a forced resettlement
tuples.time_place_scope: a population moved to land it did not know how to farm
tuples.mechanism: a knowledge loss as much as a land loss, which takes years to recover
tuples.evidence_lens: the resettlement records compared with the yields achieved

tuples.episode_object: the famine recorded in tree rings and in tax rolls at once
tuples.time_place_scope: a region with both a written and a natural archive
tuples.mechanism: a case where two independent records agree, which is rarer than it sounds
tuples.evidence_lens: the tree ring series compared with the tax remission records

tuples.episode_object: the famine that changed a country's food policy permanently
tuples.time_place_scope: a state that built a buffer stock afterwards
tuples.mechanism: the one good outcome available, and it is always bought at the same price
tuples.evidence_lens: the policy documents compared with the performance in the following shortage

coverage_profiles.subject: shipwrecks with the highest loss of life

tuples.episode_object: the overloaded ferry that capsized in calm water
tuples.time_place_scope: a route where the vessel routinely carried more than its certificate allowed
tuples.mechanism: a tolerated overloading practice, which fails on an ordinary day rather than in a storm
tuples.evidence_lens: the vessel's certificate compared with the estimated numbers aboard

tuples.episode_object: the troopship torpedoed with a full complement
tuples.time_place_scope: a wartime crossing carrying men below the waterline
tuples.mechanism: a loading arrangement that makes escape impossible for most of those aboard
tuples.evidence_lens: the loading plan compared with the survivor distribution by deck

tuples.episode_object: the emigrant ship wrecked within sight of land
tuples.time_place_scope: a coast approached at night without a reliable light
tuples.mechanism: a navigational failure at the very end of a long safe passage
tuples.evidence_lens: the light list of the period compared with the wreck position

tuples.episode_object: the passenger liner that sank faster than it could be evacuated
tuples.time_place_scope: a vessel with boats for a fraction of those aboard
tuples.mechanism: a regulation written for a smaller ship and never updated
tuples.evidence_lens: the boat capacity certificate compared with the passenger list

tuples.episode_object: the ferry that lost stability when its cargo shifted
tuples.time_place_scope: a vessel loading vehicles on an open deck
tuples.mechanism: a design vulnerability that appears only when a specific loading occurs
tuples.evidence_lens: the stability calculations compared with the loading record of the voyage

tuples.episode_object: the ship lost with no survivors and no witnesses
tuples.time_place_scope: a passage crossed in heavy weather out of sight of land
tuples.mechanism: a total loss whose cause can only ever be reconstructed, never established
tuples.evidence_lens: the wreck survey compared with the meteorological record of the night

tuples.episode_object: the vessel that sank after a collision in fog
tuples.time_place_scope: a converging traffic area with no separation scheme
tuples.mechanism: a traffic management failure, which is why separation schemes now exist
tuples.evidence_lens: the traffic survey compared with the collision inquiry findings

tuples.episode_object: the ship that burned at anchor with passengers aboard
tuples.time_place_scope: a vessel carrying a flammable cargo alongside passengers
tuples.mechanism: a stowage decision that puts fire and people in the same hull
tuples.evidence_lens: the cargo manifest compared with the fire investigation

tuples.episode_object: the ferry lost on a river crossing in flood
tuples.time_place_scope: a crossing operated in conditions well beyond its normal limits
tuples.mechanism: an operating decision made under commercial pressure
tuples.evidence_lens: the operator's records compared with the river gauge reading

tuples.episode_object: the ship wrecked on a chart error
tuples.time_place_scope: a passage relying on a survey that had never been checked
tuples.mechanism: a hazard created by paper, and corrected only after a loss
tuples.evidence_lens: the chart edition of the day compared with the modern survey

tuples.episode_object: the vessel that foundered when a hatch cover failed
tuples.time_place_scope: a cargo ship in a following sea with a heavy deck load
tuples.mechanism: a single component failure that floods a hold and ends the ship
tuples.evidence_lens: the hatch design drawings compared with the wreck damage survey

tuples.episode_object: the ship lost after a boiler explosion
tuples.time_place_scope: a vessel operating machinery beyond its safe pressure
tuples.mechanism: a maintenance and pressure decision made repeatedly until one time it fails
tuples.evidence_lens: the engineering records compared with the inquiry findings

tuples.episode_object: the ferry whose bow door was left open
tuples.time_place_scope: a route with a very short turnaround between sailings
tuples.mechanism: a procedural failure produced by schedule pressure, and found in the inquiry every time
tuples.evidence_lens: the operating procedures compared with the inquiry's timeline

tuples.episode_object: the ship that struck an uncharted rock
tuples.time_place_scope: a coast surveyed at low resolution and rarely revisited
tuples.mechanism: an information gap that persists until a hull finds it
tuples.evidence_lens: the survey history compared with the wreck position

tuples.episode_object: the vessel abandoned in ice and lost with all hands
tuples.time_place_scope: an expedition beset far from any relief
tuples.mechanism: a slow loss with a long record, which makes it unusually well documented
tuples.evidence_lens: the expedition records compared with the later search findings

tuples.episode_object: the ship lost while carrying a whole community
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement moving together on a single vessel
tuples.mechanism: a concentration of one place's population in one hull
tuples.evidence_lens: the passenger list compared with the settlement's census returns

tuples.episode_object: the vessel that sank in shallow water within reach of help
tuples.time_place_scope: a wreck close to a shore with no rescue capability
tuples.mechanism: a rescue gap rather than a distance problem, which is why lifeboat services were founded
tuples.evidence_lens: the rescue service records compared with the wreck position

tuples.episode_object: the ship overwhelmed by a single very large wave
tuples.time_place_scope: a passage across a shelf edge in a heavy swell
tuples.mechanism: a wave regime that produces occasional extremes, doubted for a century and now measured
tuples.evidence_lens: the wave measurement records compared with the loss reports from the area

tuples.episode_object: the vessel lost after ignoring a weather warning
tuples.time_place_scope: a sailing scheduled against a forecast already issued
tuples.mechanism: a decision made with the information available and against it
tuples.evidence_lens: the forecast record compared with the departure log

tuples.episode_object: the ship whose loss changed international regulation
tuples.time_place_scope: an incident that produced a new convention on safety at sea
tuples.mechanism: the one lasting product of a maritime disaster, measured in the losses that did not happen
tuples.evidence_lens: the convention text compared with the loss rates before and after

coverage_profiles.subject: mining disasters that changed the law

tuples.episode_object: the explosion that led to compulsory mine inspection
tuples.time_place_scope: a coalfield where inspection had been voluntary
tuples.mechanism: a disaster that creates a state inspectorate, which then prevents the next one
tuples.evidence_lens: the inspection statute compared with the inquiry findings

tuples.episode_object: the flood that broke through from old workings
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine driven toward abandoned galleries with no accurate plan
tuples.mechanism: a records failure, which is why accurate abandonment plans became a legal requirement
tuples.evidence_lens: the abandonment plans compared with the breakthrough point surveyed

tuples.episode_object: the fire that trapped men behind a single shaft
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine with one means of ingress and egress
tuples.mechanism: a design economy that becomes a death sentence, and is legislated against afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the mine plans compared with the second-shaft requirement that followed

tuples.episode_object: the explosion caused by an unshielded lamp
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine where naked flames were still permitted underground
tuples.mechanism: a technology available for decades and not required until people died
tuples.evidence_lens: the lamp records compared with the safety lamp regulations that followed

tuples.episode_object: the collapse of a spoil tip above a village
tuples.time_place_scope: a waste heap placed on a hillside above housing
tuples.mechanism: a siting decision whose consequence was known to engineers and not to residents
tuples.evidence_lens: the tip stability assessments compared with the tribunal findings

tuples.episode_object: the cage failure that dropped a shift down a shaft
tuples.time_place_scope: a winding system inspected on an infrequent schedule
tuples.mechanism: a maintenance interval that is longer than the component's actual life
tuples.evidence_lens: the winding gear inspection records compared with the failure analysis

tuples.episode_object: the gas outburst in a deep seam
tuples.time_place_scope: a working driven into a seam under high gas pressure
tuples.mechanism: a hazard that increases with depth, so the law has to be rewritten as mines get deeper
tuples.evidence_lens: the gas monitoring records compared with the regulation changes

tuples.episode_object: the dust explosion propagated along a roadway
tuples.time_place_scope: a dry mine where coal dust was not being suppressed
tuples.mechanism: a secondary explosion mechanism, understood only after several disasters shared the same pattern
tuples.evidence_lens: the dust sampling records compared with the propagation analysis

tuples.episode_object: the inundation from a river above a shallow working
tuples.time_place_scope: a seam worked under a watercourse with a thin cover
tuples.mechanism: a barrier thickness decision, which becomes a statutory minimum afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the cover thickness survey compared with the regulation introduced

tuples.episode_object: the disaster that produced a rescue service
tuples.time_place_scope: a coalfield with no organised underground rescue capability
tuples.mechanism: an institution created because volunteers kept dying trying to help
tuples.evidence_lens: the rescue station records compared with the inquiry recommendation

tuples.episode_object: the roof fall in an unsupported working
tuples.time_place_scope: a face advanced faster than its supports were set
tuples.mechanism: a production pressure that removes the margin, which is where most single deaths happen
tuples.evidence_lens: the support standards compared with the accident reports

tuples.episode_object: the poisoning after a fire was sealed too early
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine where the atmosphere behind a seal was not monitored
tuples.mechanism: a decision made to save the mine that costs the men still inside it
tuples.evidence_lens: the sealing decision record compared with the inquiry findings

tuples.episode_object: the explosion in a mine that had been reported unsafe
tuples.time_place_scope: a colliery where warnings had been made and filed
tuples.mechanism: a paper trail that exists, which is what makes the subsequent legislation possible
tuples.evidence_lens: the earlier complaints compared with the inquiry evidence

tuples.episode_object: the accident that ended child employment underground
tuples.time_place_scope: a workforce that included children in haulage roles
tuples.mechanism: a public reaction that legislates on age rather than on the actual hazard
tuples.evidence_lens: the employment records compared with the statute that followed

tuples.episode_object: the disaster that produced compulsory plans of workings
tuples.time_place_scope: a district where several mines worked adjacent seams
tuples.mechanism: an information requirement that protects mines from each other
tuples.evidence_lens: the surveying regulations compared with the breakthrough incidents preceding them

tuples.episode_object: the failure of a ventilation furnace
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine ventilated by a fire at the bottom of a shaft
tuples.mechanism: a ventilation method that is itself the ignition source
tuples.evidence_lens: the ventilation records compared with the mechanical fan requirement introduced

tuples.episode_object: the accident that produced a compensation scheme
tuples.time_place_scope: an industry where a death left a family with nothing
tuples.mechanism: a social insurance question raised by a disaster rather than by a principle
tuples.evidence_lens: the compensation legislation compared with the relief fund records

tuples.episode_object: the explosion in a mine using an unapproved explosive
tuples.time_place_scope: a working where blasting was done with an unsuitable charge
tuples.mechanism: a materials rule created after the fact, listing what may be used underground
tuples.evidence_lens: the explosives schedules compared with the incident reports

tuples.episode_object: the disaster that required self-rescuers to be carried
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine where men had no personal breathing protection
tuples.mechanism: a piece of equipment made compulsory by a single well-documented event
tuples.evidence_lens: the equipment regulations compared with the inquiry's medical evidence

tuples.episode_object: the accident that ended a working practice entirely
tuples.time_place_scope: a method that had been standard across a whole coalfield
tuples.mechanism: a prohibition that removes a technique rather than regulating it
tuples.evidence_lens: the method's earlier documentation compared with the prohibition order

coverage_profiles.subject: industrial accidents that poisoned a region

tuples.episode_object: the release of a heavy gas from a chemical plant at night
tuples.time_place_scope: a plant surrounded by dense housing built up around it
tuples.mechanism: a siting problem that determines the toll before the valve ever fails
tuples.evidence_lens: the plant siting approvals compared with the casualty distribution map

tuples.episode_object: the discharge of a metal compound into a bay
tuples.time_place_scope: a fishing community eating the catch from that water
tuples.mechanism: a pathway from an outfall to a dinner plate, which took decades to trace
tuples.evidence_lens: the effluent analyses compared with the clinical case series

tuples.episode_object: the tailings dam failure that reached a river system
tuples.time_place_scope: a mine storing waste behind an earth embankment upstream
tuples.mechanism: a structure whose failure mode is well understood and cheap to prevent
tuples.evidence_lens: the dam design documents compared with the downstream contamination survey

tuples.episode_object: the escape of a persistent pesticide into groundwater
tuples.time_place_scope: an agricultural district drawing drinking water from wells
tuples.mechanism: a contaminant that moves slower than the people who need to know about it
tuples.evidence_lens: the groundwater monitoring records compared with the application records

tuples.episode_object: the fire at a warehouse that put chemicals into a river
tuples.time_place_scope: an incident where the firefighting water itself carried the pollution
tuples.mechanism: a secondary release created by the response, which is rarely planned for
tuples.evidence_lens: the firewater runoff analysis compared with the downstream fish kill survey

tuples.episode_object: the smelter emissions that stripped a hillside
tuples.time_place_scope: a valley where the prevailing wind carried the plume
tuples.mechanism: a chronic release whose damage is measured in vegetation rather than in cases
tuples.evidence_lens: the vegetation survey compared with the stack emission records

tuples.episode_object: the leaded fuel deposited along a major road
tuples.time_place_scope: a corridor where soil was sampled decades afterwards
tuples.mechanism: a diffuse release with no single accident, and therefore no single moment to point at
tuples.evidence_lens: the soil sampling transect compared with the traffic volume records

tuples.episode_object: the buried waste discovered under a housing estate
tuples.time_place_scope: land redeveloped without a record of its former use
tuples.mechanism: an information failure at the point of sale, which is what land registers now exist to prevent
tuples.evidence_lens: the historic land use maps compared with the ground investigation report

tuples.episode_object: the radioactive release from a reactor fire
tuples.time_place_scope: a facility whose filters were installed as an afterthought
tuples.mechanism: a mitigation that happened to be present, which changed the scale of the consequence
tuples.evidence_lens: the filter installation records compared with the deposition survey

tuples.episode_object: the mercury released by a chlorine process
tuples.time_place_scope: an industrial site operating a cell process for decades
tuples.mechanism: a process choice whose waste is the actual product from the region's point of view
tuples.evidence_lens: the process records compared with the sediment core analyses

tuples.episode_object: the asbestos dust carried home on work clothes
tuples.time_place_scope: a town where a single factory employed most households
tuples.mechanism: a secondary exposure pathway that reaches people who never entered the building
tuples.evidence_lens: the employment records compared with the disease incidence by household

tuples.episode_object: the cyanide spill from a processing plant
tuples.time_place_scope: a river crossing several jurisdictions downstream
tuples.mechanism: a transboundary release that no single authority is responsible for
tuples.evidence_lens: the river monitoring data compared with the international notification records

tuples.episode_object: the oil released from a tanker onto a coastline
tuples.time_place_scope: a shoreline of sheltered inlets that hold oil for years
tuples.mechanism: a coastal geometry that determines how long a spill lasts
tuples.evidence_lens: the shoreline survey compared with the oil budget calculations

tuples.episode_object: the coal ash impoundment that failed into a valley
tuples.time_place_scope: a power station storing decades of ash behind a bank
tuples.mechanism: a waste volume that accumulates faster than anyone re-examines the structure holding it
tuples.evidence_lens: the impoundment inspection records compared with the failure investigation

tuples.episode_object: the solvent plume beneath an industrial estate
tuples.time_place_scope: a groundwater body used for public supply nearby
tuples.mechanism: a contaminant that travels underground for decades before it is detected
tuples.evidence_lens: the borehole monitoring series compared with the site's operating history

tuples.episode_object: the fluoride emissions that affected livestock
tuples.time_place_scope: a farming district downwind of a smelting works
tuples.mechanism: an effect noticed first in animals, which is how many industrial releases are found
tuples.evidence_lens: the veterinary records compared with the emission monitoring data

tuples.episode_object: the release that was reported only years afterwards
tuples.time_place_scope: a facility operating with limited external oversight
tuples.mechanism: a disclosure failure, which makes the health study impossible to do properly
tuples.evidence_lens: the internal records compared with the eventual public notification

tuples.episode_object: the dioxin release from a runaway reaction
tuples.time_place_scope: a chemical works in a small town in a populated valley
tuples.mechanism: a process excursion whose contamination footprint outlives the plant by generations
tuples.evidence_lens: the soil sampling grid compared with the plant's process records

tuples.episode_object: the arsenic released by historic ore processing
tuples.time_place_scope: a former mining district now used for housing and gardens
tuples.mechanism: a legacy hazard with no living responsible party, which is why the state ends up paying
tuples.evidence_lens: the historic processing records compared with the modern soil survey

tuples.episode_object: the contamination discovered by a routine water test
tuples.time_place_scope: a supply zone tested under a new statutory programme
tuples.mechanism: a hazard found by regulation rather than by illness, which is the whole point of regulation
tuples.evidence_lens: the routine monitoring returns compared with the site investigation that followed

coverage_profiles.subject: the dumbest wars ever fought

tuples.episode_object: the war that both sides believed the other had started

tuples.evidence_lens: the two national accounts compared side by side

tuples.episode_object: the war over a disputed pastry bill
tuples.time_place_scope: a foreign national seeking compensation through his government
tuples.mechanism: a private claim escalated by a state looking for a reason
tuples.evidence_lens: the diplomatic claim documents compared with the naval orders issued

tuples.episode_object: the war fought over a bucket taken from a well
tuples.time_place_scope: two cities with a long-running municipal rivalry
tuples.mechanism: a trivial theft that stands in for a century of unresolved territorial argument
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicle account compared with the earlier boundary disputes

tuples.episode_object: the war caused by a mistranslated message

tuples.evidence_lens: the original message compared with the version acted upon

tuples.episode_object: the war fought over an island nobody lived on

tuples.evidence_lens: the unit war diaries compared with the casualty returns of the night

tuples.episode_object: the war ended by a treaty nobody signed for centuries
tuples.time_place_scope: a conflict that stopped without any formal conclusion
tuples.mechanism: an administrative oversight preserved as a curiosity, and eventually corrected
tuples.evidence_lens: the archival treaty records compared with the later formal settlement

tuples.episode_object: the war fought over the ownership of a flag

tuples.episode_object: the year that set a record later broken repeatedly

tuples.episode_object: the city with an unusable harbour and no alternative

tuples.mechanism: an infrastructure sequence in which each solution creates the following problem

coverage_profiles.subject: your life and death as a soldier of an ancient army

tuples.episode_object: the fort you build before you sleep in it

evidence_expectations: Ground each entry in the kind of record named by the slot, and describe record types rather than citing any specific title, author, archive reference, or file number.
Say in every entry which statements rest on a document, which rest on later scholarship, and which rest on oral tradition alone, and never let the three blur together.
Treat a folkloric creature as a belief with a documented distribution, not as a claim about the world, and say who recorded the belief and when.
State a death toll, a date, a distance, or a price only as precisely as the record allows, and say plainly when a figure has been revised or is disputed.
Where a popular version of a story is known to be wrong, give the corrected account early and say what the popular version got right as well as what it got wrong.
State what a record could and could not establish, because in a great many of these entries that limit is the actual subject.
compatibility_rules: Pair with the counted explainer formula for the short list mode, with the second-person role formula for the six life subjects, and with the sleep history compilation formula for the long mode; the entries are written to serve all three without rewriting.
Use one subject per episode and never mix two, so an episode is one kind of thing examined twenty ways rather than an assortment.
Draw the twenty slots of a subject in any order, but never reuse a slot within one episode set, since each slot is one entry and a repeat would be the same item twice.

Do not pair with any formula that opens on a hook, builds tension across entries, promises a worst entry, or ends an entry pointing forward; the exclusions forbid all four and the material does not need them.
Do not pair the six second-person life subjects with a third-person formula, or the other forty-four with the second-person formula; the slots are written in the voice their subject requires.
